answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging every identity a sunk bond that is slashed, not refunded, when peers catch fabricated work. A fresh key enters through an inlet where it must lock collateral and pass a few graded tasks before earning any standing. Flooding ten thousand wallets therefore costs ten thousand bonds, while one honest team pays once, so fabrication stops paying. Weight follows attestations, not headcount, and each credential is an ivory token struck from the ledger on a single bad answer, so a hollow shell of puppets drains its own sponsor.
